title: Four seasonal ENSO change slopes raised tropical rain test error in two products for 1980-2025
abstract: We tested whether four fixed seasonal ENSO change slopes lower concurrent monthly rain error after month-specific curved ENSO strength and a time trend are included. We used GPCP V2.3, CMAP standard V2610 and ERSSTv5 indices for three tropical boxes in 1980-2025. Five-year blocks and adjacent years were excluded from fitting. The seasonal model raised mean squared error in all six tests, by 1.52% to 3.52%. Conditional 99.1667% three-year block intervals were below zero for error reduction in the east in both products and for the Maritime Continent in CMAP. The other three intervals included zero. The seasonal model also had higher point error than a common-change model in all six tests. Spatial index controls changed two GPCP gains to small positive values. Thus four broad seasonal slopes did not recover useful recent-change information in the primary test. This does not rule out physical memory. Shared product observations, 46 years, fixed model form and uncertainty conditional on fitted predictions limit inference. The package includes code, exact source hashes, aggregate errors, checks and a figure. Source records remain external.

display.caption: MSE reductions for four seasonal change slopes in three tropical boxes and two rain products. Negative values mean higher error. Intervals are conditional Bonferroni-adjusted circular three-year block intervals.

citations.reason: Extends its common ENSO change test with four fixed seasonal slopes and a CMAP product check. Uses the same GPCP and index snapshots.
